course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Cold War and Decolonization
unit.description: Study how the Cold War divided the world, how colonies won independence, how new states and movements challenged established power, and why the Cold War ended.

themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment
themes.question: How did geography, crops, resources, or disease shape choices?
themes.example: Andean terraces made steep slopes more usable for farming.

themes.title: Social interactions and organization
themes.question: Who had status, opportunities, or obligations?
themes.example: Examination preparation favored families that could afford education.

themes.title: Political systems and governance
themes.question: How did rulers gain authority and administer territory?
themes.example: Song officials carried imperial decisions into local government.

themes.title: Economic systems
themes.question: How were goods produced, exchanged, taxed, or distributed?
themes.example: Mali drew revenue from commerce through its territory.

themes.title: Cultural developments and interactions
themes.question: How did beliefs, learning, and artistic practices influence society?
themes.example: Buddhist monasteries connected religious practice with education.

themes.title: Technology and innovation
themes.question: What techniques or tools changed what people could do?

questions.prompt: Which two states emerged as superpowers after World War II?
choices: Britain and France, the war's European victors
The United States and the Soviet Union
Germany and Japan after their reconstruction
The United States and Great Britain
questions.explanation: Only the United States and the Soviet Union had the military and economic strength to dominate the postwar world.
choiceExplanations: Britain and France won but were weakened and indebted.
Only the United States and the Soviet Union had the military and economic strength to dominate the postwar world.
Germany and Japan were defeated and occupied.
Britain was a close US ally but too indebted to remain a superpower.
questions.distinguisher: Britain was on the winning side but did not have superpower strength after 1945.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best explains why the wartime alliance between the United States and the Soviet Union broke down after 1945?
choices: The Soviet Union had refused to fight Germany until the war's final months
The two powers fought a border war in Europe in 1946
Without a common enemy, their opposing systems and goals clashed
Both states were too weakened by the war to help rebuild Europe
questions.explanation: Once Germany was defeated, capitalist democracy and Soviet communism competed for influence.
choiceExplanations: The Soviet Union bore the heaviest share of the fighting against Germany.
The superpowers never fought a war against each other, in 1946 or later.
Once Germany was defeated, capitalist democracy and Soviet communism competed for influence.
Both emerged far stronger than the European powers.
questions.distinguisher: The superpowers were the two strongest states, not the weakest.

questions.prompt: Which of the following was a way World War II encouraged decolonization?
choices: It left Britain and France richer and better able to pay for their empires
It led Asian nationalists to abandon demands for independence
Japan's early victories showed European colonial powers could be beaten
It gave colonial powers large new armies to hold their colonies by force
questions.explanation: Japan's conquests of 1941 and 1942 broke the image of European invincibility.
choiceExplanations: Britain and France ended the war deeply in debt.
Nationalist movements grew stronger after the war.
Japan's conquests of 1941 and 1942 broke the image of European invincibility.
The colonial powers were exhausted and demobilizing.
questions.distinguisher: Britain and France were on the winning side, but the war weakened their economies.

questions.prompt: Nationalist demands for self-determination after 1945 are best understood in the context of
choices: the Atlantic Charter and colonial subjects' wartime service
the Congress of Vienna's restoration of monarchs
the Berlin Conference's division of Africa
the Treaty of Versailles granting independence to all colonies
questions.explanation: Colonial peoples who had fought for the Allies cited the Charter's promise of self-government.
choiceExplanations: Colonial peoples who had fought for the Allies cited the Charter's promise of self-government.
The Congress of Vienna met in 1815 to restore European monarchies.
The Berlin Conference of 1884 divided Africa among colonizers.
The 1919 settlement created mandates rather than freeing colonies.
questions.distinguisher: The 1919 peace spoke of self-determination but applied it only in Europe.

questions.prompt: The structure of the United Nations Security Council reflected the postwar world because
choices: it excluded every country that had fought in the war
it gave the war's main victors permanent seats and a veto
it gave colonies an equal vote with their rulers
it gave every member nation a permanent seat and a veto
questions.explanation: The United States, the Soviet Union, Britain, France, and China held permanent seats.
choiceExplanations: The founders were the war's victors.
The United States, the Soviet Union, Britain, France, and China held permanent seats.
Colonies were not members.
Only five members hold permanent seats with a veto.
questions.distinguisher: The veto belongs only to the five permanent members, not to every member.

questions.prompt: Which piece of evidence from the passage best supports the claim that the United States emerged from the war in a strong position?
choices: Fifty nations met in San Francisco to found the United Nations
Britain and France, its allies, were deeply in debt after the war
It produced about half of the world's manufactured goods
Millions of refugees were on the move across Europe and Asia
questions.explanation: Economic output on that scale shows American strength in 1945.
choiceExplanations: The San Francisco meeting shows cooperation, not American strength.
That describes the weakness of other powers rather than US strength.
Economic output on that scale shows American strength in 1945.
Refugees show the war's destruction.
questions.distinguisher: European debt shows others' weakness; the question asks for evidence of US strength.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 8.1 key concept: World War II weakened the European powers and left the United States and the Soviet Union as rival superpowers
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the world in 1945
stimulusBlocks.text:
In 1945, much of Europe and East Asia lay in ruins. Cities from Warsaw to Tokyo had been bombed, and millions of refugees were on the move. Britain and France had won the war but were deeply in debt.

The United States, untouched by fighting at home, produced about half of the world's manufactured goods and alone possessed the atomic bomb. The Soviet Union had lost about 27 million people, but its armies occupied Eastern Europe. Fifty nations met in San Francisco that year to found the United Nations, hoping to prevent another world war.

questions.prompt: The founding of the United Nations described in the passage is best understood as a response to
choices: the failure of the League of Nations to prevent World War II
the League of Nations' success in stopping aggression in the 1930s
the Communist victory in China's civil war in 1949
the collapse of the Soviet Union and its Eastern European allies
questions.explanation: The founders hoped a stronger organization would succeed where the League had failed.
choiceExplanations: The founders hoped a stronger organization would succeed where the League had failed.
The League failed to stop aggression in the 1930s.
The UN was founded in 1945, four years before the communist victory in China.
The Soviet Union was a founding member.
questions.distinguisher: The League existed in the 1930s, but it failed rather than succeeded.

questions.prompt: The Soviet occupation of Eastern Europe described in the passage most directly contributed to
choices: the immediate independence of Eastern European states
tension between the Soviet Union and the Western powers
the end of the Soviet Communist Party
the Soviet Union's withdrawal of its troops from all of Eastern Europe in 1946
questions.explanation: Western leaders saw Soviet-backed governments in Eastern Europe as a threat.
choiceExplanations: Eastern European states came under Soviet-backed governments.
Western leaders saw Soviet-backed governments in Eastern Europe as a threat.
The Communist Party ruled the Soviet Union until 1991.
Soviet troops stayed in Eastern Europe for decades.
questions.distinguisher: Soviet troops remained in Eastern Europe until the end of the Cold War.

questions.prompt: The passage suggests that the Atlantic Charter
choices: brought an immediate end to British rule in India
was written by Asian and African nationalist leaders
was used by nationalists to challenge colonial rule
was rejected by nationalists as irrelevant to colonies
questions.explanation: Nationalists quoted its promise of self-government back to the colonizers.
choiceExplanations: India won independence in 1947, six years later.
Britain and the United States issued it.
Nationalists quoted its promise of self-government back to the colonizers.
Nationalists embraced its words.
questions.distinguisher: The Charter fed nationalist demands, but India's independence came later.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 8.1 key concept: World War II weakened colonial empires and strengthened demands for independence
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing how World War II weakened colonial empires
stimulusBlocks.text:
Japan's conquest of Malaya, Singapore, the Dutch East Indies, and Burma in 1941 and 1942 shattered the image of European power in Asia. About 2.5 million Indians served in the British Indian Army during the war, and hundreds of thousands of Africans fought for Britain and France.

In the Atlantic Charter of 1941, Britain and the United States declared that all peoples had the right to choose their own government. Nationalist leaders across Asia and Africa quoted those words back to the colonial powers after the war.

questions.prompt: The passage would best support which argument?
choices: World War II strengthened colonial rule in Asia
Colonial subjects played no role in World War II
World War II weakened the foundations of colonial rule
Japan's conquests made Europeans more secure
questions.explanation: Japanese victories, colonial service, and the Charter all undermined imperial authority.
choiceExplanations: The passage describes colonial power being shaken.
Millions of Indians and Africans served.
Japanese victories, colonial service, and the Charter all undermined imperial authority.
Japan's victories shattered European prestige.
questions.distinguisher: Japan's victories in Asia undermined European colonial rule rather than strengthening it.
